overview: Four-month feasibility pilot (January to April 2027) of a laboratory hold rule for HbA1c requests within 80 days of the previous result in six primary care practices, with progression criteria for network rollout and a safety review of held requests.
population: All HbA1c requests from six practices: three from the highest decile of early repeat requesting and three typical practices, of mixed size and rurality; requests from hospitals are excluded.
exposure: Hold rule: a request within 80 days is held and a one-sentence comment explains the retesting interval and gives the override route (reply code with a reason: pregnancy, new diagnosis, recent transfusion or blood loss, treatment change in the last 8 weeks, other).
procedures: The rule is switched on for the six practices only after network committee agreement. Every hold and override is logged by the laboratory information system. A diabetologist and a practice pharmacist review every held request followed by a treatment change within 30 days, every override without an accepted reason, and a random 10 percent of other holds. Requesters complete a five-question acceptability survey in month four. Progression criteria are fixed before the rule starts.

outcomes.name: Timely overrides for accepted exceptions
outcomes.measure: Proportion of overrides for accepted exceptions completed within one working day of the hold
outcomes.why: Decides whether patients who need a test get it without delay; progression threshold 90 percent.

outcomes.name: Held requests that delayed an important decision
outcomes.measure: Number judged by the two reviewers to have delayed a clinically important decision
outcomes.why: The committee's safety condition; progression threshold zero.

outcomes.name: Rule firing and override rates
outcomes.measure: Holds per 100 HbA1c requests and overrides per 100 holds, with reasons
outcomes.why: Workload and plausibility of the rule settings.

outcomes.name: Requester acceptability
outcomes.measure: Proportion rating the comment clear and acceptable on the five-question survey; progression threshold 60 percent
outcomes.why: Acceptability was the main risk in the retrieved evidence.

outcomes.name: Second blood draws after an override
outcomes.measure: Overridden holds that required the patient to attend again
outcomes.why: Burden on patients who travel far or need interpreters.

feasibility: About 3,000 HbA1c requests are expected from the six practices in four months, with about 540 holds and 60 overrides; the safety review is about 8 hours a month of reviewer time within existing roles.
biasMitigation: Progression criteria fixed before the rule starts
Reviewers use a written definition of an important delay
Practices chosen by pre-specified rules, not volunteering alone

biasFlags.label: Small numbers for overrides
biasFlags.note: About 60 overrides give an interval of roughly 8 points around 90 percent.

biasFlags.label: Hawthorne effect in pilot practices
biasFlags.note: Practices may change requesting because they know they are observed.

flags: Progression thresholds rather than hypothesis tests
Two process and two balancing measures
parsimony.simplestPath: One rule, six practices, four months, four progression thresholds.

theoreticalFramework: No framework beyond feasibility progression criteria; acceptability questions follow a simple five-item structure.
summary: Four-month pilot in six practices with four progression criteria and a safety review.
